I just started homebrewing because one of my favorite alcohols is Mead, but Mead is super expensive. Well when visiting my local meadery I learned another thing about Mead, it's super easy to make :D

Given Voats do-it-yourself attitude; what better place to talk about making your own alcohol: From mead, to fruit wine, to beer, to rum. What do you like to brew?

Equipment you need:

  • 2 gallon glass jugs (you can buy them or get 2 4 liter wine jugs and sterilize them)

  • Airlock and stopper (Google if you don't know, should cost $5 at most)

  • Syphon hose (brew shops sell em)

  • Sanstar sterilizer, but if you are cheap use a water/bleach mix

  • Wine bottles or beer bottle for bottling. whatever floats your goat

Basic first ever mead: (Aprox $15.15 a gallon)

  • 1 gallon distilled water ($0.88)

  • 3 lbs clover honey ($10.00)

  • 1/2 a spoon of cinnamon ($0.01)

  • 1/2 a spoon of nutmeg ($0.01)

  • 1/2lb of brown sugar ($3.00)

  • 1 pack of champaign yeast ($1.25)

How to Make

  1. Sterilize/sterlize (bacteria ruins your alcohol), then add honey (all of it) nutmeg, 1/2 lb of brown sugar and cinnamon. (Save your honey jar)

  2. Next add most of the distilled watter but give your self a good amount of space to shake the jug. (don't use all your distilled water)

  3. Then, shake for 10 minutes. If you did it right, all honey and stuff should be disolved.

  4. After that, take that honey jar you emptied out add the distilled water to it and shake it up like you did the jug

  5. Then add the yeast to the honey jar, this is to get the yeast acclimated. VERY gentilely shake or swivel around. Wait 15ish to 45 ish minutes

  6. Finally add yeast to jug, gently movie the yeast around in the jug, pop on your airlock and wait 2 months.

After 2 months, use a syphon hose to get all the clear liquid and leave behind the gunk at the bottom behind and put the good stuff in the other gallon jug. Age to your liking, then syphon into wine bottles. To carbonate add a spoon of processed white sugar to the bottom before adding mead in the bottle. cork it up, age and enjoy.
